title: August and the Visitor
premise: Ada Dunmore, a pest controller with twelve years of rational explanations behind them, is called to a farmhouse where the excavation crew has unearthed a door sealed from the inside — and something with fingerprints. Trapped overnight with the crew, Ada discovers the house was built as a cage for a thing that feeds on memory, and that the family who invited it in made a bargain: one keeper per generation must surrender their past to keep it contained. As the creature strips the others of who they are, Ada realizes the door was sealed from the inside by the last keeper — still alive, still remembering nothing but the lock. At dawn, Ada chooses to take up the bargain themselves, trading every memory of their found family to reseal the door, surviving at the price of never knowing why they stayed.
about_author: August Quintana is the pen name of a former rural building inspector who spent a decade documenting structures that should not have existed. They write horror about ordinary people whose competence becomes their undoing.

chapters.title: The Callout
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A routine pest-control callout to the Harrow farm turns strange when Ada finds claw-marks that end in human fingerprints. Twelve years of rational explanations begin to crack as they inspect a cellar wall that hums when touched. Emotional beat: professional denial meeting the first undeniable evidence.

chapters.title: What the Excavator Found
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, joined briefly by foreman Denny Ruiz. The excavation crew unearths an iron door set into bedrock beneath the barn, its hinges rusted shut — sealed from the inside. That night, the crew refuses to leave; the road out loops back on itself. Emotional beat: dread shifting from curiosity to entrapment.

chapters.title: Fingerprints
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The fingerprints multiply across every surface overnight, always slightly wrong — too many whorls, pressed too hard. Crew member Sal Okafor touches one and forgets her daughter's name mid-sentence. Ada recognizes the pattern from old farm ledgers: this has happened before, in cycles. Emotional beat: the horror acquires rules.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In the farmhouse attic, Ada finds generations of journals describing 'the tenant' and the bargain: one keeper surrenders their memories each generation to keep it fed and locked. The last entry, dated forty years ago, is written in a shaking hand that stops mid-word. Emotional beat: hope curdling into inheritance.

chapters.title: Sal Forgets the Sky
chapters.summary: Alternating Ada and Sal POV. Sal deteriorates rapidly, losing language, then faces, then her own reflection. The others try to hold onto her with stories, forming a fragile found-family bond around her erasure. Ada secretly writes down everything they know about each person — insurance against forgetting. Emotional beat: tenderness under siege.

chapters.title: The Man Behind the Door
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Following the humming wall, Ada finds a crawl space and meets Elias Harrow — alive, ancient, remembering nothing but the lock he has turned every night for four decades. He begs Ada not to open the door, then begs them to, unable to recall which he wants. Emotional beat: pity for the monster's jailer, who is also its victim.

chapters.title: Denny's Bargain
chapters.summary: Denny Ruiz's POV. Desperate to save his crew, Denny attempts his own deal with the thing behind the door, offering memories freely. It takes too much — he forgets why he's holding a crowbar, then that he ever had a crew. Ada drags him back, realizing the bargain only holds if given willingly and completely. Emotional beat: the price of half-measures.

chapters.title: Sunrise Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Dawn approaches but the loop outside holds; sunrise won't come until the tenant is satisfied or resealed. Ada counts what remains: three minds intact, one dying keeper, one door. They realize the original seal required a keeper who chose it knowing exactly what they'd lose — which is why Elias's half-remembered turning is failing. Emotional beat: the terrible clarity of the arithmetic.

chapters.title: Everything I Know About You
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada reads aloud the pages they wrote about Sal, Denny, and the crew — giving everyone back their names one last time before walking down to the door. Elias shows them how the lock works: it turns from the inside only, by someone who remembers what they are giving up. Emotional beat: love expressed as inventory, farewell disguised as ritual.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, final pages in stripped-down second person. Ada enters, turns the lock, and lets the tenant take all of it — the crew, the farm, the twelve years of noises explained. Sunrise breaks. Outside, a pest controller wakes in their van with no callout on the books, only a notebook full of strangers' names and an ache like a missing tooth. Emotional beat: survival achieved, selfhood paid; the reader knows what Ada no longer can.
